clue.text: Farm hand producing lower output

parts.note: a lower is something that lows, a cow, and its output is milk, so this farm worker draws milk from cattle

explanation.surface: A farm labourer whose productivity has dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' reads as 'less', but it is one that lows, a cow; the hand's output is the cow's milk.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional female farm worker whose job was hand-milking the cows of the dairy.

clue.text: One MP has variable ill-fortune

indicators.note: something variable changes its form, so these letters are shifted into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Member of Parliament whose luck keeps changing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variable' rearranges I (one) with MP and HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A small accident or bad luck event is a synonym for ill-fortune in a minor instance.

clue.text: Pulse found in virulent illnesses

indicators.note: the letters are found within the words that follow, running across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A heartbeat detected in patients with severe diseases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks medical beside the illnesses, but it is the edible seed; 'found in' spans virulENT ILlnesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are edible legume seeds, and this small lens-shaped seed is one of them.

clue.text: One that always pockets litter

parts.note: litter is a brood of young, and this animal carries its young in a pouch

explanation.surface: Someone who habitually picks up rubbish and stuffs it in their pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' suggests rubbish, but it is newborn young, held in a pouch like a kangaroo's.
explanation.definitionFit: Kangaroos, wallabies and koalas are pouched mammals that rear their young in a pocket of skin.

clue.text: They try to get opinions among TV audiences

parts.note: inter is a Latin-derived prefix meaning among or between
people watching television are viewers

explanation.surface: Pollsters canvassing views from television viewers.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists and pollsters who question people seek their views and opinions.

clue.text: How to make do?

parts.note: read as how to make someone do something, that is, how to force them

explanation.surface: A question about managing with little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make do' suggests getting by with what you have; read instead as 'make (someone) do', which is to force.
explanation.definitionFit: To force or oblige someone to act is a synonym of making them do it.

clue.text: Sea air adds a little weight to one

parts.note: oz, an ounce, is a small unit of weight
taken as written

explanation.surface: Seaside air makes a person put on a bit of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Popularly, the bracing smell of the seaside is credited to this form of oxygen.

clue.text: An order you'll carry out, if you can!

definitions.text: An order you'll carry out, if you can!

parts.words: An order you'll carry out, if you can!
parts.note: the instruction to keep food from spoiling is carried out by putting it in a can, a tin

explanation.surface: A command you'll obey if you're able.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if you can' sounds like 'if you're able', but can means tin: canning keeps food.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep food from decay, as jam or tinned fruit is kept, is to protect it from spoiling.

clue.text: An accommodating woman

parts.note: accommodating here means providing lodgings rather than being obliging

explanation.surface: A woman who is obliging and easy to please.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodating' suggests helpful, but here it means giving people rooms to stay in.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who lets rooms to lodgers or runs a pub provides accommodation.

clue.text: When this foreign girl gets married, she loses it

definitions.text: When this foreign girl gets married, she loses it

parts.words: When this foreign girl gets married, she loses it
parts.note: the Spanish title for a young unmarried woman becomes the one for a wife by dropping the letters I and T

explanation.surface: A racy hint about what a foreign bride gives up on her wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' hints at virtue, but literally the letters IT go: the Spanish miss's title becomes señora, a married lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish for Miss, a young unmarried woman, whose married counterpart is señora.

clue.text: Nobly involved with English queen who lost her head

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A noble English queen who was beheaded, tangled up in court intrigue.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne, second wife of Henry VIII, was executed by beheading in 1536 at the Tower of London.

clue.text: One made to move on cue

definitions.text: One made to move on cue

parts.words: One made to move on cue
parts.note: a cue is the stick in a table game, which strikes this object to set it rolling

explanation.surface: An actor trained to step forward on a prompt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on cue' suggests a theatrical prompt, but the cue is the stick used on a baize table.
explanation.definitionFit: The ivory or resin spheres struck with a cue in the game played on a green cloth table.

clue.text: So long to suffer in a university

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other, so the suffering word goes inside the two letters

parts.note: to die is to suffer the ultimate fate

explanation.surface: Bidding farewell to hardship at college.
explanation.definitionFit: A French-derived farewell, equivalent to goodbye, said when parting.

clue.text: Make a disturbance to give a lift to the underworld

definitions.meaning: to cause an uproar or a fuss

definitions.text: give a lift to the underworld
definitions.meaning: taken literally, to raise or lift the infernal regions

explanation.surface: Causing chaos by hoisting up the realm of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for creating an uproar, here also read literally as lifting Hades upward.

clue.text: Upset when given an open transfer?

definitions.text: Upset when given an open transfer?

parts.words: Upset when given an open transfer?
parts.note: taken literally, being shifted in full view of everyone, as a footballer might be on transfer

explanation.surface: A footballer distressed at being put up for sale publicly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' is the real sense; the transfer is read literally as moving someone where all can see.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing emotion plainly is an idiom for being upset, read literally as relocated in view.

clue.text: The state you're in after the match

definitions.text: The state you're in after the match

parts.words: The state you're in after the match
parts.note: match here means a marriage pairing, not a sporting fixture

explanation.surface: How you feel once the game is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests a game, but it is a marriage; the state that follows is wedlock.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedlock, the condition of being married, is the state a couple enters.

clue.text: Snooty head of a religious order

definitions.meaning: the person in charge of a convent or monastery, as in Mother of the house

explanation.surface: A stuck-up abbess or abbot.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: an arrogant, haughty manner, and the title of the leader of a monastic house.

clue.text: Shoot like this and you'll probably miss

definitions.text: Shoot like this and you'll probably miss

parts.words: Shoot like this and you'll probably miss
parts.note: firing without aim or plan, haphazardly, rarely hits the target

explanation.surface: Advice to a marksman about poor technique.
explanation.definitionFit: Haphazardly, without method or aim, as a shot fired anyhow.

clue.text: Large sum not declared, apparently

definitions.meaning: an immense fortune, riches beyond counting
read literally, riches not told, that is, kept from the tax authorities

explanation.surface: A big amount of money hidden from the taxman.
explanation.definitionFit: Vast riches too great to be counted, here read literally as money never told about.

clue.text: Go back to bed?

definitions.meaning: to go to bed for the night

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: withdrawing or retreating, and turning in for the night to sleep.

clue.text: Holds 150 serpents

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals
asps are venomous snakes

explanation.surface: A snake charmer keeps a huge number of snakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Grips or fastenings that hold things together, as a verb meaning grasps.

clue.text: Fascinated by unusual demeanour

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary form, so these letters take a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Captivated by someone's odd manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Charmed or captivated, in love with someone or something.

clue.text: Go round the globe on it

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so the globe comes first

parts.note: an orb is a sphere or globe

explanation.surface: An instruction to travel round the world.
explanation.definitionFit: To circle a planet or star in a fixed path, as a satellite does.

clue.text: Thought first of ladies a model of excellence

parts.note: an idea is a thought

indicators.note: the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: An opinion that the leading women are paragons.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect standard or exemplar worth aiming for, a paragon.

clue.text: Descriptive of one who can't settle

definitions.text: Descriptive of one who can't settle

parts.words: Descriptive of one who can't settle
parts.note: settle here means pay off a bill, not calm down

explanation.surface: Describing a restless person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settle' suggests calming down, but it means paying up: such a person owes money.
explanation.definitionFit: Owing money and unable to clear one's accounts, a state of owing.

clue.text: Covers with article inside various editions

indicators.note: the article goes inside the editions word

parts.note: copies are the individual issues of a print run
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Book jackets that come with an extra piece in different versions.
explanation.definitionFit: Overhead coverings or awnings, such as those above a bed or throne.

clue.text: Nowhere near being unapproachable

explanation.surface: Someone cold and distant, far off.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: physically far away, and aloof or standoffish in manner.

clue.text: Games enclosures for the very young

definitions.text: Games enclosures for the very young

parts.words: Games enclosures for the very young
parts.note: pens, small fenced areas, in which toddlers play safely

explanation.surface: Sports grounds designed for children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Games enclosures' suggests sports grounds; read it as play plus pens, fenced spaces for babies.
explanation.definitionFit: Portable barred frames inside which babies and toddlers can be safely left to amuse themselves.
